'''Eddy Anthony Curry Jr.'''<ref>{{Cite web|title=Eddy Curry Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/curryed01.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=2020-05-25}}</ref> (born December 5, 1982)<ref name="Heat bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/roster/heat_player_eddy_curry_1112.html|title=Eddy Curry Bio|work=Miami Heat |access-date=June 25, 2013}}</ref> is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. A 7 ft 0 in (2.13 m) [[Center (basketball)|center]], he came directly out of [[Thornwood High School]] in [[South Holland, Illinois]], and was selected fourth overall in the [[2001 NBA draft]] by the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Curry played for the Bulls until 2005, then played for the [[New York Knicks]] from 2005 to 2010. He played for the [[Miami Heat]] in the {{nbay|2011}} season and was part of the Heat's [[2012 NBA Finals|2012 championship team]]. He played for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the early part of the {{nbay|2012}} season before playing out the season for the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].

==High school career==
Prior to becoming considered one of the best high school basketball players in the nation as a senior at [[Thornwood High School]] in [[South Holland, Illinois]], Curry aspired to be a [[Gymnastics|gymnast]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://proxy.espn.com/espn/page2/story?page=jackson/051011|title=ESPN.com: Page 2 : Heart of the Eddy Curry matter|website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> and did not pick up basketball until the seventh grade when he reluctantly went out for the school team. In 2001, Curry led his team to second place in the [[Illinois High School Association|IHSA]] State Playoffs. For his efforts, Curry was named 2001 [[Illinois Mr. Basketball]]. In his senior year of high school he posted averages of 22 points per game, 9 rebounds and 6 blocks.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/draft2001/playerfiles/eddy_curry.html?nav=ArticleList Player Profiles – Eddy Curry], [[NBA.com]].</ref> He was named to the 1998, 1999 and 2000 State Farm Holiday Classic all-tournament teams, and in 2003 was named by the fans to the tournament's All-Quarter Century Team.

In 2001, Eddy Curry and four other high school basketball stars, were the subject of the documentary "Preps: Chicago Hoops", a series about making the jump to college or the NBA.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0309202/|title=Preps: Chicago Hoops (TV Series 2001– ) – IMDb|date=February 4, 2001|via=www.imdb.com}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Chicago Bulls (2001–2005)===
Curry had signed a letter of intent to play at [[DePaul University]] but declared himself eligible for the [[2001 NBA draft]] in which the [[Chicago Bulls]] made him the fourth overall pick.

Curry's contribution was limited during his rookie year due to limited minutes. Curry improved in his second year, leading the NBA in [[Field goal (basketball)|field goal]] percentage (58.5%) and becoming the first Bull to lead the league in a major statistical category since [[Michael Jordan]] in 1998. In the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]] the Bulls improved by 28 wins and made the [[NBA Playoffs|playoffs]] as the 22-year-old Curry led the team in scoring before being hospitalized with an irregular heartbeat. This caused him to miss the last 13 games of the regular season and the entire playoffs. On June 24, 2005, heart specialists cleared Curry to resume practice.

===New York Knicks (2005–2011)===
[[File:CurryNYK.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Curry attempts a shot in a January 2007 game against the [[Washington Wizards]].]]

On October 3, 2005, after refusing on privacy grounds to submit to a [[DNA]] test, as requested by Bulls management, to assess whether he has a congenital heart condition, Curry was traded to the New York Knicks. The trade included the Bulls' [[Antonio Davis]], as well as the Knicks' [[Michael Sweetney|Mike Sweetney]], [[Tim Thomas (basketball)|Tim Thomas]], and [[Jermaine Jackson (basketball)|Jermaine Jackson]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/bulls/news/curry_traded_051004.html Bulls Re-Sign Curry, Complete Sign-and-Trade with Knicks], National Basketball Association, accessed January 14, 2009.</ref> First-round draft picks were also exchanged in the trade—which later came back to haunt the Knicks as they had a poor 2005–06 season in which Curry averaged 13.6 points and 6.0 rebounds per game (numbers that were significantly down from the previous season). Curry's inability to defend and rebound was a source of frustration for former coaches [[Scott Skiles]] and [[Larry Brown (basketball)|Larry Brown]]. When asked by a reporter in 2003 what Curry needed to do to become a better rebounder, Skiles simply replied: "Jump."<ref>[http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/story/360620p-307293c.html New York Sports – NY Daily News<!-- Bot generated title -->] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060629013237/http://www.nydailynews.com/sports/story/360620p-307293c.html |date=June 29, 2006 }}, ''[[Daily News (New York)|New York Daily News]]'', accessed January 14, 2009.</ref> The [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]] saw a resurgence in Curry's performance under new coach [[Isiah Thomas]], with Curry anointed the team's primary offensive option, averaging career highs in points (19.6), rebounds (7.1), and minutes (34.9) per game. On April 7, 2007, Curry scored a career-best 43 points in an overtime win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]; his first [[three-point field goal|three-pointer]] of the season forcing the game into the extra period.<ref name="knicksbucks">[https://web.archive.org/web/20190201120153/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270407015 Curry nets 43, grabs 13 boards and forces OT with 3-pointer], [[ESPN]], April 8, 2007, accessed January 14, 2009.</ref> Curry is 2 for 2 (100%) from three-point range in his NBA career.<ref name="knicksbucks" /> In the 2007–2008 season, Curry was expected to form a great frontcourt with [[Zach Randolph]], however both of them saw a regression in their games. Curry showed up to training camp in October 2008 out of shape for the second year in a row, incensing new head coach [[Mike D'Antoni]]. Curry not only lost his starting job, but was not even in D'Antoni's rotation at the beginning of the 2008–2009 season. Curry was also bothered by a sore right knee for much of the season. Curry played his first game of the season on January 8, 2009, against the [[Dallas Mavericks]] and played in two other games later in the season.
During the 2009 off-season Curry began working with a trainer on a fitness and weight-loss regimen. As of mid-July he had lost 30 pounds, but according to the trainer it would be "delusional" for coaches to think he could get down to his listed weight of 285 pounds.<ref>Alan Hahn, [https://web.archive.org/web/20090717092137/http://www.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/ny-spknix1412966225jul13,0,5194704.story Trainer: Don't expect Curry to slim down to 285], July 13, 2009</ref>

=== Miami Heat (2011–2012) ===
On February 22, 2011, Curry was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in a three-way blockbuster deal which also involved [[Denver Nuggets]] that brought [[Carmelo Anthony]] to New York.<ref>{{cite web | title = Wolves Acquire Anthony Randolph | url = http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/pressrelease_Wolves_Acquire_Anthony_Randolph_2011_02_22.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = February 22, 2011 | access-date = February 23, 2011}}</ref> On March 1, 2011, his contract was bought out by the Timberwolves<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=6173198 "Wolves buy out center Eddy Curry"], [[Associated Press]] at [[ESPN.com]], March 2, 2011.</ref> before he played a single game for them, making him a free agent.

On December 10, 2011, Curry signed a one-year contract with the Miami Heat.<ref>{{cite web | title = HEAT Signs Eddy Curry | url = http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_signs_eddy_curry_111210.html | work = [[NBA.com]] | date = December 10, 2011 | access-date = January 20, 2012}}</ref> On January 19, 2012, a noticeably-slimmer Curry played in the NBA for the first time since 2009, against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He had lost nearly 70 pounds since he last played in the NBA, and scored six points in six minutes in his return to the NBA.<ref>[[Dan LeBatard]], [http://www.miamiherald.com/2012/01/22/2601178/miami-heats-eddy-curry-back-in.html "Miami Heat’s Eddy Curry back in shape with help from Dwyane Wade, LeBron James"], ''[[Miami Herald]]'', January 22, 2012.</ref> As a part of the Heat's 2011–2012 championship team, Curry played 83 minutes<ref>Ethan J. Skolnick, [http://blogs.palmbeachpost.com/heatzone/2012/06/14/eddy-curry-anxiously-awaits-the-summer/ "Eddy Curry anxiously awaits the summer"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120617110040/http://blogs.palmbeachpost.com/heatzone/2012/06/14/eddy-curry-anxiously-awaits-the-summer/ |date=June 17, 2012 }}, ''[[Palm Beach Post]]'', June 14, 2012.</ref> in 14 games (starting one), and was active for (but did not play in) one game during the playoffs.<ref>Ira Winderman, [https://web.archive.org/web/20130720225809/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2012-05-25/sports/sfl-miami-heat-eddy-curry-s052412_1_active-roster-inactive-list-dexter-pittman "Eddy Curry on active roster Thursday, does not play"], ''[[South Florida Sun Sentinel]]'', May 25, 2012.</ref>

=== Dallas Mavericks (2012) ===
In October 2012, Curry signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/121001_spurs_add_two_training_camp_roster|title=Spurs Add Two To Training Camp Roster|website=San Antonio Spurs}}</ref> However, he did not make the team's final roster.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/121023_waive_brown_curry|title=Spurs Waive Derrick Brown and Eddy Curry|website=San Antonio Spurs}}</ref>

Curry was claimed off waivers by the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on October 25, 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11286|title=Dallas Mavericks sign center Eddy Curry via waiver claim – NBA Blog |date=October 25, 2012 }}</ref> He played two games for Dallas before being waived to make room for [[Troy Murphy]], as the Mavericks wanted a power forward with outside shooting ability instead of a traditional center.<ref>{{cite web|author=Tim MacMahon |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/mavericks/post/_/id/4692407/mavs-make-troy-murphy-eddy-curry-moves-official |title=Mavs make Troy Murphy, Eddy Curry moves official |work=ESPN |date=November 2, 2012 |access-date=May 18, 2013}}</ref> The second game that Curry played for Dallas on October 31, 2012, ended up being his final NBA game ever. In his final game, Curry and the Mavericks would lose to the Utah Jazz 94 - 113 with Curry recording 2 points and no other stats in 8 minutes of play.

===Zhejiang Golden Bulls (2012–2013)===
On December 6, 2012, Curry signed with the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] in China, replacing [[Josh Boone (basketball)|Josh Boone]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://niubball.com/2012/12/zhejiang-chouzhou-replaces-josh-boone-with-eddy-curry/|title=| Zhejiang Chouzhou replaces Josh Boone with Eddy CurryNiuBBall.com}}</ref> Curry played in 29 games and averaged 23.0 points, 10.1 rebounds, and 0.9 assists per game.<ref name="asia basket">{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/index.aspx|title=Eddy Curry Player Profile, Killers 3s, News, Stats – Asia-Basket|website=Eurobasket LLC}}</ref> Curry played his last game with Zhejiang on February 27, 2013,<ref name="asia basket"/> as he missed the last two playoff games due to [[gastroenteritis]].<ref>{{cite web|title=CBA |script-title=zh:埃迪-科里患肠胃炎，浙江单外援出战季后赛|url=http://voice.hupu.com/cba/1340442.html|publisher=Hupu.com|access-date=December 27, 2013|language=zh|date=February 28, 2013}}</ref>

===Zhuhai Wolf Warriors (2018–2019)===
Curry signed with the [[Macau Wolf Warriors|Zhuhai Wolf Warriors]] of the [[ASEAN Basketball League]] (ABL) in 2018, and played for the team in the [[2018–19 ABL season]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Justin Taguibao |url=http://aseansports.com/index.php/2018/10/17/wolf-warriors-reveal-abl-roster/ |title=Zhuhai Wolf Warriors Reveal ABL Roster |work=ASEANSports |date=October 17, 2018 |access-date=November 18, 2018}}</ref> He was released by the Wolf Warriors on January 20, 2019.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hoang |first1=Jayden |title=Wolf Warriors Replaces Eddy Curry |url=http://aseansports.com/basketball/wolf-warriors-bid-farewell-to-eddy-curry/ |website=ASEAN Sports |access-date=July 27, 2020 |date=January 20, 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Curry is married and has seven children, one from a previous marriage (Eddy III), and four with his current wife Patrice Curry, who starred on [[VH1]]'s ''[[Basketball Wives LA]]'' franchise.<ref>{{cite web|title=VH1|url=http://www.vh1.com/celebrities/patrice-curry/#cast=basketball_wives_la|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150625050848/http://www.vh1.com/celebrities/patrice-curry#cast=basketball_wives_la|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 25, 2015|access-date=July 1, 2015}}</ref> Curry's other two children, Ava and Noah, were with former girlfriend Nova Henry, who was murdered in 2009 along with 10-month-old Ava.

===Cardiac problems===
Several prominent cardiologists cleared Curry to play,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Isola |first=Frank |date=2005-10-30 |title=Laying It On The Line. Convinced heart is fine, Curry embraces Knicks |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2005/10/30/laying-it-on-the-line-convinced-heart-is-fine-curry-embraces-knicks/ |access-date=2025-03-30 |website=[[New York Daily News]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>Kathryn Kranhold and Kevin Helliker, [https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB115378816415916014 "Why Heart Trouble Doesn't Sideline Some Athletes: Dr. Cannom Helps Players Benched by Their Schools; Defibrillators and Testing Drawing the Line at Football"], ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'', July 25, 2006</ref> but Barry Maron, a world-renowned specialist in [[hypertrophic cardiomyopathy]], suggested a [[DNA]] test.<ref>[http://www.medpagetoday.com/Cardiology/Arrhythmias/tb/1843 Medical News: Full Court Press on Hoop Star Curry to Get DNA Testing – in Cardiovascular, Arrhythmias from MedPage Today<!-- Bot generated title -->], MedPage Today, accessed January 14, 2009.</ref> During the team's media day, Bulls General Manager [[John Paxson]] said he understood the privacy issues involved but insisted the Bulls did not have an ulterior motive, that their concern was a situation similar to those of former [[Boston Celtics]] guard [[Reggie Lewis]] or [[Loyola Marymount University|Loyola Marymount]] star [[Hank Gathers]]—players with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy who collapsed and died—and that the Bulls had offered Curry an annuity of $400,000 per year for 50 years if he took and failed the genetic test.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2180298 "Bulls deal Curry after DNA test refusal"], [[Associated Press]] at [[ESPN.com]], October 4, 2005.</ref>  Curry never took the test and ultimately continued his career based on the clearances from other experts.<ref>Darren Rovell, [https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2340042 "Sources: NBA to standardize physicals"], [[ESPN.com]], February 27, 2006.</ref>

===Alleged sexual harassment===
On January 12, 2009, Curry was sued by his former [[chauffeur]], David Kuchinsky. Kuchinsky accused Curry of trying to solicit sex from him. According to court papers, Curry twice approached Kuchinsky "in the nude," saying, "Look at me, Dave, look" and, "Come and touch it, Dave." Kuchinsky also alleged that Curry called him racial slurs.<ref>{{cite web|last=Evans|first=Patrice|title=Eddy Curry Hit With Gay Sex Harassment Suit|url=http://www.nbcchicago.com/news/sports/Eddy-Curry-Charged-With-Being-More-Offensive-Off-The-Court-Than-On-It.html|publisher=WMAQ (NBC Chicago)|access-date=June 25, 2013|date=January 14, 2009}}</ref>

Kuchinsky claimed Curry owed him $68,000 in unpaid wages, as well as $25,000 in expenses which Curry never repaid. Those expenses, he said, included cellphones that Curry had him buy as gifts and hotel and club bills.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.nypost.com/seven/01132009/news/regionalnews/knick_gets_called_for_sex_foul_149982.htm | work=New York Post | title=Knick Gets Called For Sex Foul | date=January 13, 2009}}</ref>  Curry's lawyer, Kelly A. Saindon, called Kuchinsky's claims "preposterous" and "extortion".<ref>Howard Beck,[https://www.nytimes.com/2009/01/13/sports/basketball/13eddy.html "Driver Sues Curry for Sexual Harassment"], ''[[The New York Times]]'', January 12, 2009.</ref> Federal judge [[Denise Cote]] dismissed the lawsuit on May 28, 2009, and sent it to [[arbitration]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Beck|first=Howard|title=Lawsuit Against Knicks' Curry Will Be Settled by Arbitrator|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/05/29/sports/basketball/29knicks.html|work=The New York Times|access-date=June 28, 2013|date=May 29, 2009}}</ref>

===Daughter's and ex-girlfriend's murders===
Curry's ex-girlfriend, Nova Henry, and their ten-month-old daughter Ava Curry were found murdered in [[Chicago]] on January 24, 2009. A paternity test proved that Ava was the daughter of Curry and Henry. Their three-year-old son Noah was found unharmed at the scene.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3868735 New York's Eddy Curry Was Father of Slain Baby] ESPN.com, January 28, 2009, accessed January 30, 2009.</ref> Two counts of first degree murder were brought against 36-year-old [[Lawyer|attorney]] Frederick Goings on February 22, 2009;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3926761&campaign=rss&source=NBAHeadlines |title=Man charged in death of Eddy Curry's ex, their baby – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=February 22, 2009 |access-date=November 2, 2012}}</ref> Goings had served as Henry's attorney in a custody case against Curry involving Ava, and was allegedly involved in a relationship with Henry.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20090226134310/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/basketball/nba/02/22/curry.charges.ap/index.html Charges in Death of Eddy Curry's Ex-Girlfriend, Baby] SI.com, February 23, 2009</ref>  Goings was convicted of all charges against him on February 12, 2013,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.suntimes.com/news/18189197-418/lawyer-guilty-of-killing-former-chicago-bull-eddy-currys-ex-girlfriend-daughter.html|title=Lawyer guilty of killing former Chicago Bull Eddy Curry's ex-girlfriend, daughter}}</ref> and was sentenced to life in prison two months later.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://abc7news.com/archive/9053298/|title=Frederick Goings sentenced to life in prison murder of Nova Henry, baby Ava}}</ref>

===Foreclosure===
As of June 2009, Curry's Chicago home was in [[foreclosure]]; he owed close to $220,000 in [[Mortgage loan|mortgage]] payments. Curry took out a nearly $4 million mortgage on the property in 2006, which included monthly house payments of more than $25,000.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://blogs.suntimes.com/sportsprose/2009/06/eddy_currys_suburban_mansion_i.html |title=Eddy Curry's suburban mansion in foreclosure - Sports Pros(e) |website=blogs.suntimes.com |access-date=13 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090703111413/http://blogs.suntimes.com/sportsprose/2009/06/eddy_currys_suburban_mansion_i.html |archive-date=3 July 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>
[http://weblogs.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/blog/2009/06/eddys_financial_issues_continu.html Eddy's financial issues continue] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090703113748/http://weblogs.newsday.com/sports/basketball/knicks/blog/2009/06/eddys_financial_issues_continu.html |date=July 3, 2009 }}</ref> In June 2021, Curry was evicted for violating his lease agreement in Katy, Texas. {{Citation needed|date=July 2021}}

==Awards and accomplishments==

===High school===
* ''[[USA Today]]'' First Team [[All-America]]n
* ''[[Parade (magazine)|PARADE]]'' High School Player of the Year
* Earned [[Illinois Mr. Basketball]] honors
* MVP of the [[McDonald's All-American]] game after scoring 28 points with 8 rebounds and 4 blocked shots in leading the West to a 131–125 victory
* Led Thornwood High School to the Illinois State Championship game, averaging 22.0 points, 9.0 rebounds and 6.0 blocked shots, shooting .640 from the floor, including 25.0 points and 10.0 rebounds in the state tournament. Averaged 24.6 points and 11.2 rebounds, along with 4.8 blocks, as a junior.
* Was selected to the State Farm Holiday Classic all-tournament team in 1998, 1999 and 2000.
